newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Khmer Rouge say Cambodia's Hun Sen should be tried.
newsitem.headline: Khmer Rouge say Cambodia's Hun Sen should be tried.

text.p: The Khmer Rouge guerrilla group said on Monday Cambodian leader Hun Sen should be brought before an international court for the alleged killing of supporters of the man he ousted as co-premier last month.
"The puppet Hun Sen has to be sent to the international court and sentenced in accordance with his criminal act," guerrilla radio said in a broadcast monitored in Phnom Penh.
The guerrillas' clandestine radio has long been their main propaganda mouthpiece.
Second Prime Minister Hun Sen ousted his senior co-premier, Prince Norodom Ranariddh, on July 6 after two days of fighting in the capital.
Subsequently some 40 of the prince's supporters, including several senior military officials and their bodyguards, were killed, diplomatic sources and human rights workers said.
Government officials said one senior royalist official was executed after he was taken into custody and at least one other was killed in the fighting. But the government denied human rights abuses.
Khmer Rouge guerrillas, who purged their notorious leader Pol Pot late last month, have repeatedly criticised Hun Sen for ousting Ranariddh.

The rebels have labelled Hun Sen a puppet of Vietnam and have called for united opposition to his rule, while Hun Sen has warned of military action against the rebels in their Anlong Veng base in the remote north of the country.
Many members of the royalist FUNCINPEC party and its sympathisers left Cambodia after Ranariddh's overthrow, including some 20 members of parliament.

Hun Sen at the weekend accused a United Nations human rights office in Phnom Penh of frightening people into fleeing the country. The office has been investigating reports of human rights abuses and helped some Cambodians leave the country.
Hun Sen appealed to members of parliament and others who had left Cambodia to return and resume their political activities.
